security_audit.summary: The 58 static external-command findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code and fenced code blocks, not executable backtick use. No prompt injection or malicious automation was found. One medium semantic issue remains because the REST API example uses an unrestricted permission callback.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted REST API permission callback in example code
remediation.suggestion: Replace __return_true with a capability or nonce based permission callback, or clearly state when a public GET endpoint is acceptable.

remediation.issue: Production hardening guidance for sample WordPress code
remediation.suggestion: Add a note that examples need sanitization, escaping, validation, and access-control review before production use.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted WordPress REST Endpoint Example
semantic_findings.description: The custom REST API example registers a route with permission_callback set to __return_true. This allows anonymous access and can teach unsafe access control if copied for non-public data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly uses __return_true on a REST route. The route is GET and may be public by design, so the finding is medium severity rather than high.

content.user_title: Build WordPress Projects With Guided Workflows
content.value_statement: WordPress projects span themes, plugins, performance, security, and deployment. This skill organizes each phase into practical actions and prompts.
actual_capabilities: Guides WordPress setup, theme development, plugin work, WooCommerce, testing, and deployment.
Lists related skills to invoke during each workflow phase.
Provides copy-paste prompts for AI handoffs between specialized development tasks.
Shows example WordPress theme and plugin directory structures.
Includes basic PHP examples for post types, REST routes, and WooCommerce products.
Provides checklists for performance, security, and release quality gates.
limitations: Does not run WordPress commands or modify project files by itself.
Sample code is illustrative and needs review before production use.
Depends on referenced skills that may not exist in every environment.
Does not replace official WordPress, WooCommerce, or payment documentation.

use_cases.title: Launch a WordPress Build
use_cases.description: Plan setup, theme structure, plugins, quality gates, and deployment tasks for a new site.

use_cases.title: Plan a Custom Plugin
use_cases.description: Break plugin work into architecture, hooks, admin screens, REST endpoints, and tests.

use_cases.title: Prepare a WooCommerce Release
use_cases.description: Coordinate payment integration, checkout changes, subscriptions, performance, and security checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a New Site
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a first WordPress build
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the WordPress workflow to plan a new local WordPress project. Include setup, theme choice, required plugins, and first checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Theme Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the WordPress workflow to outline a custom theme build. Include template files, component work, styling, accessibility, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Performance and Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the WordPress workflow to create a performance and security review plan. Include caching, updates, headers, authentication, and logging checks.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Full Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the WordPress workflow to build a launch plan for a WooCommerce site. Include development, payments, testing, deployment, rollback, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Plan a custom WordPress theme for a service business.
output_examples.output: A phased build plan covering setup, theme structure, responsive templates, performance checks, security checks, and launch readiness.

output_examples.input: Create a workflow for a WooCommerce subscription store.
output_examples.output: A release checklist for products, payment setup, checkout customization, subscription logic, testing, deployment, and post-launch monitoring.

output_examples.input: Audit a WordPress site before production launch.
output_examples.output: A quality gate review covering updates, authentication, headers, file permissions, backups, performance metrics, browser tests, and accessibility.

best_practices: Verify each generated WordPress change in a local or staging environment first.
Review examples for nonce checks, capability checks, sanitization, and escaping.
Use the phase checklists before moving from development to deployment.
anti_patterns: Treating copy-paste prompts as production-ready implementation without review.
Publishing sample API endpoints without explicit access-control decisions.
Skipping WordPress core, theme, and plugin updates before security testing.

faq.question: Does this skill build WordPress sites automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured workflow, prompts, examples, and checklists for guided development.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include WooCommerce guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers WooCommerce setup, checkout customization, payments, subscriptions, and release checks.

faq.question: Are the PHP snippets production ready?
faq.answer: No. They are examples and require security, validation, and access-control review.

faq.question: What project phases does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers setup, theme development, plugin development, WooCommerce, performance, security, testing, and deployment.

faq.question: Does it replace WordPress documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it as workflow guidance alongside official WordPress and WooCommerce documentation.
